posts.cooked:
Hi all!

We’re a busy family in Los Angeles. We’d like to work with an independent engineer or a small studio to set up a private, dependable home system that uses AI to help run our household: calendars, notes, documents, email drafts, and a knowledge base we actually use. Privacy matters a lot to us, so sensitive documents should be handled on a machine in our house, with cloud AI used where it makes sense.

It starts as a defined project. If it goes well, it turns into a light ongoing relationship: a check-in twice a year to keep things healthy and add new capabilities as the tools improve.

What we have in mind (very open to your suggestions):

  • A Mac mini at home running local models (Ollama or LM Studio) for private document search and processing
  • Claude API / Claude Code for scheduling help, translation and workflow logic
  • n8n for automation (our preference), or Google Apps Script / small custom services if they fit better
  • Notion (family contacts, projects, how-to docs) alongside Google Workspace
  • Meeting notes from Fathom or Granola

What we’d like help with:

  1. Design how our data moves between the home machine and the cloud, and what stays where
  2. Build the automations: meeting notes, a shared family calendar, document processing, and email drafts
  3. Write it all up in a plain-language “household runbook” so we’re never stuck
  4. After that, a twice-a-year retainer: health checks, rotating keys, and carefully adding new AI tools

You’d be a great fit if you:

  • Have built real integrations with Notion, Google Workspace and a workflow tool like n8n
  • Have run local LLMs and know their practical limits (context windows, speed, quality)
  • Care about privacy, encryption and systems that fail gracefully (good logging, automatic recovery)
  • Are happy to sign an NDA
  • Like explaining things clearly and working directly with non-engineers

A bit about us: we’re a family of four, with two young kids who are curious and very talkative. We lived in New York for 15+ years. We have down-to-earth Midwestern values and a global outlook (my wife is from Jakarta and my dad immigrated from India). We try to do what we say, and we’d love to work with someone who does the same.

Budget: $1,000-2,000 for a paid first phase to get us set up. If that goes well, the rest of the build and the twice-a-year retainer would follow. We’d love to hear what you’d tackle first in that range.

Location: Los Angeles, remote is fine, with an occasional visit.

If you’re interested, reply here or email 37jn5k7ti@mozmail.com with an n8n project you’re proud of. Happy to answer questions in the thread.

posts.name: Cindy Garcia
posts.cooked:
Hi, I’m Cindy. I read this twice, because it is basically the system I already run for my own business, just pointed at a household instead of a company.

Here is what I would spend that first phase on, and it is not the local model.

I would start with the boring plumbing. Where your data lives, what never leaves the house, and one loop your family actually uses every day. In the $1,000 to $2,000 range I would do the data map, then meeting notes turning into action items, calendar entries and draft emails, with you approving anything before it gets sent. Then the runbook. I would build the private document search on the Mac mini second, once you can see what is really in those files. Local search is the piece that eats the most time and disappoints people the fastest if you aim it at everything at once.

On local models, the limit people underestimate is not quality, it is patience. Something that answers in eight seconds gets used. Something that takes a minute gets abandoned by month two and everybody quietly goes back to texting each other.

One thing I would build in from the first day is that every job tells you when it fails. I learned that one the hard way. My own system caught something important and I did not find out for six days, because the alert only landed on my desktop and I was not at my desk. Now everything emails me. In a house with two kids, quiet has to mean it worked, not that nobody was watching.

Also, twice a year is plenty for adding new capability, but it is not enough for keys. Google tokens and API keys expire on their own schedule, so I would have the system test its own connections weekly and email you before something stops working, instead of you finding out in June that it stopped in March.

I am a nurse, so writing things down in a way a normal person can follow at 10pm is honestly the part I am best at.

Happy to answer anything here, and I am glad to walk you through what I run for myself if you want something concrete to look at.

Cindy Garcia

  2. One end-to-end loop you’ll actually use daily, meeting notes to action items to a calendar entry and a draft email, with your approval before anything sends
  3. A plain-language runbook so none of it is a black box

An n8n project I’m proud of: a documentation pipeline that watches a source system, classifies and reformats updates with AI, and pushes clean pages into a team’s knowledge base with no manual editing — same pattern your household knowledge base would need. A four-node n8n workflow built with disclosed AI assistance and executed locally in n8n 2.38.7. It uses six synthetic events, normalizes email case/whitespace, validates positive units, ignores identical repeated event IDs, and preserves conflicting duplicates and invalid rows for review.
